_comment: THE INCLUDE LIST for the 3D page, and the source of truth for what it
loads. The page fetches exactly this -- no candidate list, no directory
scan -- so adding a provider to the browser runtime is an edit here and
nothing else. Load order is the order these appear in.
WindowProvider first because a Surface takes its handle from a live window;
RenderProvider is the one this page exists for; ShellProvider last so the
navigator comes up in the embedded terminal.
PAINTPROVIDER IS ABSENT, and that is the point of having this page at all:
the 3D path should stand up with nothing from the 2D editor loaded, and a
page that quietly depended on it would not show that.
_scripts: Staged into the browser's filesystem by the page, under these names, before
main() runs -- so each one must also answer over HTTP (../serve_scene3d.etcs
mounts them). A NAME MAY BE A PATH: the page creates the directories first
(FS.mkdirTree), which is what lets a script be staged at the same relative
path the OS side reads it from, so scene3d.etcs's `detach` and `run` lines
are spelled once for both substrates rather than twice.
RenderProvider/scripts/scene3d.etcs is the GEOMETRY -- the reusable scene
this page's boot script runs against its own anchor. Two files named
scene3d.etcs, at two paths, because they are two jobs: one builds structure,
the other stands up a session around it.
_glue: The emscripten loader output, STAGED AS .js: served extensionless it arrives
as application/octet-stream, which the browser warns is not a valid
